extracted.intended_audience: scholars and students of philosophy and humor studies; academics interested in subversive/political humor
extracted.subtask_description: A philosophical analysis of incongruity, seriousness, and playfulness as they relate to humor generally and to subversive/political humor in particular; explains what makes some incongruities amusing and how humor can be used to challenge injustice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incongruity as source of laughter
rubrics_metrics.description: “Laughter always arises from nothing other than a suddenly perceived lack of congruence between a concept and the real objects that are in some respect or other thought through it...” (Schopenhauer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: an amusing event requires a perceived mismatch between an expected conceptual schema and the concrete situation. Note: Schopenhauer locates laughter in recognition of incongruity but does not by itself explain why some incongruities produce mirth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not all incongruities are humorous
rubrics_metrics.description: Some incongruities (e.g., the grotesque, the macabre, the horrible, the bizarre, the fantastic) do not elicit mirth; an incongruity can be disturbing rather than amusing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating humor, distinguish amusing incongruity from threatening/disturbing incongruity (example: finding a severed head is incongruous but not funny). Consider emotional valence and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Play mode / cognitive shift required for amusement
rubrics_metrics.description: Morreall: laughter arises from a sudden conceptual shift caused by recognition of a non-threatening incongruity—moving from a serious state of perceiving to a nonserious/playful state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: the audience must be able to adopt a play mode (cognitive distance) to find the incongruity pleasurable. Assess whether a piece fosters or demands that shift.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-threatening character of humorous incongruity
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor requires that the incongruity be perceived as non-threatening so it can be enjoyed rather than provoking fear, disgust, or other practical emotions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether the target or context invokes practical danger or urgent needs; if so, amusement is unlikely. Non-threat is a necessary condition for mirth in this account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional/practical engagement undermines humor
rubrics_metrics.description: Emotions such as fear, pity, indignation, disgust, or practical concerns orient one toward urgent actions and thus reduce pleasure sufficient for humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the content elicits practical/emotional engagement; high practical engagement counts against being experienced as humorous under Morreall’s model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience mental state matters (ignorance/confusion vs playfulness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Incongruity is only enjoyable for those 'who are ignorant and confused' in a play mode; ignorance/confusion can be pleasurable when one is in play mode rather than seeking immediate resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether intended audience is encouraged to linger in confusion playfully rather than forced into rapid problem-solving or anxiety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cognitive flexibility / openness (anti-epistemic-closure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor (especially subversive humor) requires and fosters cognitive shifting and openness; it opposes 'epistemic closure' and convergent thinking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: a successful humorous intervention should invite alternative perspectives and unusual connections rather than reinforce fixed categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subversive humor: serious play (combining playfulness with concern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subversive humor uses playful incongruity to attack unjust status quos; it is playfully presented yet seriously aimed at change—'serious play.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging subversive humor, look for a combination of playful style and a substantive target/commitment (the humorist cares about the issue even while playing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience capacity and inclination to cognitive shifting
rubrics_metrics.description: For subversive humor to work, the audience must have both the ability and the inclination to shift perspectives and enter a playful interpretive mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess target audience readiness; the humorist may need to prompt or scaffold playfulness to make the subversive point effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humor can convey serious/illocutionary content indirectly
rubrics_metrics.description: Jokes and non-bona-fide language may be taken as conveying meaningful moral/political assertions even if not literal—humor can have illocutionary and perlocutionary effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume play = no communicative intent. Evaluate whether the humorous remark functions to persuade, criticize, or mobilize despite its non-literal surface.

rubrics_metrics.name: Devices of subversive humor: hyperbole, implicature, counterfactuals, role-reversal
rubrics_metrics.description: Subversive wit often employs hyperbole, implicature (conveying more than literal content), counterfactuals, and socio-political role-reversals to reveal incongruities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In analysis or production, identify and assess these rhetorical devices as tools to generate pleasing incongruity and reveal critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functions/benefits of (subversive) humor
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor can (1) focus attention on what is wrong and spark resistance, (2) create solidarity among those laughing together at oppressors, and (3) serve a coping function to help the oppressed endure suffering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate humor by which of these functions it plausibly fulfills and whether it balances them ethically (e.g., does it encourage resistance rather than mere escapism?).

rubrics_metrics.name: Humor as instrument for habituating detection of incongruities
rubrics_metrics.description: Amusement in detecting incongruities habituates audiences to look for more incongruities—serving as intellectual training for confronting uncertainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether humor cultivates long-term critical sensitivity or merely provides transient pleasure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivation of playfulness (not default)
rubrics_metrics.description: Play mode is not the default mental state; it must be cultivated (like taste), and educational/social practices (e.g., imaginative play) foster it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the context or creator encourages developing playfulness (e.g., framing, cues) rather than presuming it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambiguity of 'seriousness' — three senses
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper distinguishes three meanings of seriousness: (1) existential (Schopenhauer), (2) Morreall’s solemn/practical engagement (grave, earnest), and (3) the sense that something 'matters' to an individual (concern/commitment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analyzing or crafting humor (especially subversive), clarify which sense of seriousness is in play and how humor relates to that sense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical limits: oppressive/harmful jokes and the problem of 'just playing'
rubrics_metrics.description: Morreall’s account risks exonerating oppressors who claim 'just playing' and undermining marginalized peoples’ subversive humor by classifying it as mere frivolity; racist/sexist jokes can present stereotypes that some audiences take as true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate harmful potential: consider power dynamics, who is targeted, whether stereotypes are reinforced, and whether play-signals actually prevent harm to marginalized groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humor often violates Gricean conversational maxims
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor commonly breaks cooperative principles (do not say what you believe false; avoid ambiguity; be orderly/brief)—these violations can be part of how jokes function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use awareness of Gricean violations to analyze how a joke signals non-bona-fide intent and how those signals might succeed or fail across audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pleasure in humor as 'victory of perception over thought' (insight)
rubrics_metrics.description: Schopenhauer: the pleasure of laughter is the 'victory of knowledge of perception over thought'—seeing reason convicted of insufficiency yields delight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the humorous moment produces a satisfying insight/reversal for the audience (an epistemic pleasure), not merely shock.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk of trivialization vs potential for change
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor can either trivialize suffering (aestheticize oppression) or function as practical non-violent protest; subversive humor aims at the latter by highlighting contingencies rather than inevitabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether humor trivializes important issues or instead opens possibilities for critique and change; look for evidence of practical engagement or mere escapism.
